create.title: Discrete nondegeneracy of actual M2 dyadic weights

update.statement_tex: With the audited Vaaler coefficient alpha_{h,H}=-Phi(|h|/(H+1))/(2 pi i h), the M2 coefficient beta_{h,H}=alpha_{h,H}(e(h/4)-e(3h/4)) equals -Phi(|h|/(H+1)) chi_4(|h|) 1_{2 not divides h}/(pi |h|). Hence beta_{h,H} is real and even, and |beta_{1,H}|>=1/(2 pi) for H>=1.
update.reason_for_promotion: The source coefficient is now audited and the modulo-4 evaluation of e(h/4)-e(3h/4) was independently checked.

update.statement_tex: Assuming the matching exact N=0 absolute mass closure, H_D>=1, and either a sharp dyadic block or actual weights supported in a fixed shell with sum_d |w_D(d)| >= lambda D, the unit-frequency W-1 family satisfies Sigma_abs(0<|N|<=M) >= c min(D^4,MD)-C_epsilon D^2 X^epsilon. At M=D^4/X this refutes Sigma_abs <<_epsilon D^2 X^epsilon for D>=X^(1/3+delta), after choosing epsilon<3delta. This is an absolute or genuinely unsigned obstruction only, not a signed estimate; the exact crossover D=X^(1/3) is not a power contradiction.
update.next_action: Treat character-blind absolute control as impossible by a power for D>=X^(1/3+delta). Verify the actual dyadic l1 normalization, then pursue a sign-preserving M2 estimate from the X^(1/3) crossover upward.
Preserve chi_4(h) in signed lift, signed energy, or direct bilinear estimates. Do not use character-blind absolute norms in the power-obstructed range D>=X^(1/3+delta).

reject.reason: Bounded smooth weights may vanish or have o(D) sampled l1 mass; smoothness alone cannot transfer the sharp W-1 lower bound.
A positive h=1 subtotal does not lower-bound the full signed sum because complementary frequency tuples can cancel it.
At D=X^(1/3) the W-1 main term is only of order D^2, so there is no power separation from D^2 X^epsilon.
